POSITION TITLE: Director of Philanthropy

SALARY LEVEL: $80,000 – $100,000

INCENTIVE COMPENSATION: This position is eligible for a performance-based incentive equal to
2% of every full $100,000 in qualifying new funds generated through
the Director of Philanthropy's efforts. Incentive compensation is
contingent upon achievement of fundraising goals and
organizational performance targets established at the start of each
fiscal year. Incentive eligibility requires active employment in good
standing at the time of distribution.

JOB DEFINITION: The Director of Philanthropy provides strategic leadership for the
organization’s fundraising and development function, designing and
executing a comprehensive philanthropic program to sustain and
grow the organization’s mission and programs. As a member of the
senior leadership team, this role sets the long-term development
vision and strategy, establishes annual fundraising goals in
partnership with the CEO, and provides monthly performance
updates to track progress toward these goals. The Director leads
the annual campaign, cultivates and stewards the organization’s
most significant donor relationships in close partnership with the
CEO and Board, and holds overall accountability for all aspects of
development, including donor stewardship, major and planned gifts,
corporate and foundation partnerships, grants, and signature
fundraising events. The Director also builds, leads, and develops
the development team.

REPORTS TO: CEO

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor’s degree in Nonprofit Management, Business
Administration, Humanities or a related field; advanced degree or
CFRE certification preferred. 7+ years of progressive leadership
experience in nonprofit development, including a proven record of
personally securing major and principal gifts, leading
comprehensive fundraising programs, and building and managing
high-performing development teams. Demonstrated success setting
fundraising strategy and meeting or exceeding multi-million-dollar
revenue goals. Proficiency with donor database management,
moves management, and data analysis. Working knowledge of
current federal (IRS) and state (CA) rules and regulations governing
charitable giving. Must successfully complete a criminal background
check prior to employment. Once employed, must complete an 80-
hour training to become a certified Domestic Violence/Sexual
Assault Counselor.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

•    Set the organization’s long-term development strategy and establish annual fundraising goals with input from the CEO, ensure alignment with organizational priorities, and provide monthly updates on performance to plan.
•    Design, direct, and execute the organization’s annual campaign, integrating direct mail, digital outreach, personal solicitations, and events to maximize donor engagement and revenue.
•    Partner with the CEO and Board to establish and deepen relationships with donors, focusing on building connections between donors and WRC’s leadership, mission, and programs.
•    Personally manage a portfolio of major donors and prospects; identify, cultivate, solicit, and secure six- and seven-figure gifts from individual, corporate, and foundation donors, while expanding the donor base.
•    Develop and oversee a robust donor stewardship program, ensuring meaningful recognition and fostering long-term donor relationships.
•    Build, lead, mentor, and develop the development team, setting performance expectations and fostering a culture of philanthropy across the organization.
•    Oversee the planning and execution of major fundraising events including the annual gala.
•    Partner with the CEO and program leaders to identify funding opportunities, align initiatives, and engage board members in fundraising efforts.
•    Direct the creation of compelling fundraising materials, represent WRC at public events and donor meetings, and organize tours and informational gatherings to inspire donor support.
•    Leverage donor management systems to track performance metrics, analyze trends, and inform strategic decision-making to optimize fundraising results.
•    Develop and manage the development department budget.
•    Other duties as assigned.

OTHER:

•    Comply with General Agency Responsibilities
•    At all times demonstrate the ability to work well under pressure, meeting multiple and sometimes conflicting deadlines
•    At all times demonstrate cooperative behavior with colleagues, clients, volunteers, supervisor and administrators

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER:

WRC is an equal opportunity employer committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. No person shall be discriminated against due to race, color, age, religion, sex, marital status, physical handicap, pregnancy, ancestry, national origin, veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Overview

Since our founding in 1924, we've cut cardiovascular disease deaths in half, but there is still so much more to do. To overcome today’s biggest health challenges and accelerate this progress, we need passionate individuals like you. Join our movement, be part of the progress, and help ensure a healthier future for all. You matter, and so does the impact you can make with us.

We are currently hiring a Development Director in Los Angeles. The Development Director will generate revenue for our Heart Walk fundraising campaign. This campaign includes our signature Los Angeles Heart & Stroke Walk event.

This hybrid position is based in the Los Angeles County division and the work is wherever it is most effective – in the field, at home and in our Culver City office.

We have a fast-paced sales type of environment with the main responsibility of driving revenue in support of our mission. We offer a base salary with the potential to earn an incentive up to 25% of your base pay. The potential incentive is based on achieving certain revenue targets and triggers.

The Association offers many resources to help you maintain work-life harmonization through your changing needs and life situations. To help you be successful, you will have access to Heart U, our award-winning corporate university, as well as additional training and support, locally.

\#TheAHALife is more than a company culture; it is our way of life. It embodies our commitment to work-life harmonization and is guided by our core values where our employees can thrive both personally and professionally. Discover why you will Be Seen. Be Heard. Be Valued at the American Heart Association by following us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, and at heart.jobs.

Responsibilities

Generate revenue by prospecting and securing local corporate sponsorship and individual donations. Achieve revenue goals by building and maintaining relationships with corporate partners and donors.
Build and maintain a pipeline of prospective corporate sponsors and donors by conducting research that matches to the campaign goals and the Association's mission.
Develop and present proposals and accompanying materials to secure revenue and volunteer engagement.
Recruit and be responsible for executive volunteer leadership, volunteer committees, and day-of-the-event volunteers.
Recruit corporate team participation in Heart Walk and motivate team members to fundraise.
Lead and engage new individual membership for our Cor Vitae giving society, in partnership with other appropriate fundraising staff. Includes planning and implementing regular engagement events for members.
Plan and implement events in collaboration with internal and external partners.
Work with a Communications Director to support and promote campaign communication plans.

Qualifications

3 years of relevant experience in fundraising, sales, or other related experience
University/College degree or equivalent experience
Ability to do daily local travel and some overnight trips as needed; requires access to reliable transportation at all times on an immediate basis
Ability to lift and/or move large objects (such as boxes) with the expectation that heavier items would be broken down into smaller components or requesting additional assistance may be required before lifting and/or moving
Must have at least basic knowledge and skill/proficiency with Microsoft Office

Here are some of the preferred experience and skills we are seeking:

Experience managing and cultivating high-level leaders at the C-Suite level
Knowledge of corporate and community networks

Compensation & Benefits

Expected pay range will be $70,725 to $83,000 annually. Pay is commensurate with experience; geographic differentials to the pay range may apply. The American Heart Association reserves the right to pay more or less than the posted range.

The American Heart Association invests in its people. Here are the main components of our total rewards package. Visit Rewards & Benefits to see more details.

Compensation – Our goal is to ensure you have a competitive base salary. That’s why we regularly review the market value of jobs and make adjustments, as needed.
Performance and Recognition – You are rewarded for achieving success through annual salary planning and incentive programs;this position is incentive eligible based on achieving certain targets.
Benefits – We offer a wide array of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance, along with a robust retirement program that includes an employer match and automatic contribution. As a mark of our commitment to employee well-being, we also offer an employee assistance program, employee wellness program and telemedicine, and medical consultation.
Professional Development – You can join one of our many Employee Resource Groups (ERG) or be a mentor/mentee in our professional mentoring program. Heart U is the Association’s national online university, with more than 100,000 resources designed to meet your needs and busy schedule.
Work-Life Harmonization – The Association offers Paid Time Off (PTO) at a minimum of 16 days per year for new employees. The number of days will increase based on seniority level. You will also have a total of 12 paid holidays off each year, which includes several days off at the end of the year.
Tuition Assistance - We support the career development of all employees. This program provides financial assistance to employees who wish to further their education and career in relation to their current duties and responsibilities, or for potential future positions in the organization.

The American Heart Association’s 2028 Goal: Building on over 100 years of trusted leadership in cardiovascular and brain health, by 2028 the Association will drive breakthroughs and implement proven solutions in science, policy, and care for healthier people and communities. The greatest discoveries in health must reach everyone where they are.

At American Heart Association | American Stroke Association, our mission is to be a relentless force for a world of longer, healthier lives, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, religion, age, language, sexual orientation, national origin and physical or cognitive abilities.

Founded in 1886, Natividad has served Monterey County for 140 years and remains one of the region's most important public institutions. The 172-bed hospital is supported by nearly 1,700 employees and more than 400 physicians and medical staff. Each year, Natividad records approximately 60,000 emergency department visits, more than 11,000 inpatient admissions and nearly 2,200 births.

Natividad is fully accredited by The Joint Commission and is one of California's 17 public health care systems. It serves as Monterey County's essential safety net hospital, its only teaching hospital and one of the Central Coast's most important providers of advanced and lifesaving care.

The hospital operates the only Level II Trauma Center in Monterey County, providing 24-hour access to trauma-specialized care and treating approximately 1,400 trauma patients annually. Natividad also offers nationally recognized women's and children's services, a Level III Neonatal Intensive Care Unit affiliated with UCSF Benioff Children's Hospitals, acute rehabilitation, behavioral health, surgical and specialty care, comprehensive primary care and Monterey County's only child maltreatment clinic.

Natividad's longstanding academic affiliation with the University of California, San Francisco is central to its mission. Its nationally recognized UCSF-affiliated Family Medicine Residency is one of the university's original affiliate residency programs and prepares physicians to serve medically underserved communities, advance health equity and become leaders in family medicine.

Natividad is owned and operated by County of Monterey and governed by the County of Monterey Board of Supervisors, with guidance from a Board of Trustees. The Hospital Chief Executive Officer reports directly to the Board of Supervisors and works closely with the Board of Trustees, county leadership, elected officials, labor representatives, community partners and other stakeholders. The CEO will lead an executive team that includes the Chief Medical Officer, Chief Nursing Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Information Officer and Assistant Hospital Administrators.

The incoming CEO will inherit a highly regarded public hospital with a strong financial foundation, a committed workforce and a culture deeply rooted in quality, compassion and service. This is not a mandate to redefine Natividad's identity. Rather, the next CEO will maintain and enhance the organization's strengths while positioning it to respond to a rapidly changing health care, financial and political environment.

The CEO will provide strategic, operational and financial leadership for the hospital and will be responsible for advancing high-quality patient care, long-term sustainability, workforce engagement, regulatory compliance and community impact. The successful candidate will balance fiscal discipline with thoughtful investment, identify opportunities to responsibly grow the organization's reach and strengthen Natividad's position as a trusted provider of choice throughout Monterey County.

This role requires a politically astute and highly collaborative executive who can operate effectively within a visible public-sector governance structure. The CEO must be comfortable working across two boards and building trusted relationships with county officials, legislators, medical staff, employees, organized labor, community leaders, donors and regional health care partners. The successful candidate will be credible in the boardroom, effective in the community and able to communicate clearly in an environment where decisions are subject to public scrutiny.

The Board is seeking a forward-looking leader who can translate vision into action and bring stakeholders together around meaningful change. The next CEO will have the opportunity to advance the patient experience, strengthen access and care coordination, support strategic investments in technology and facilities, attract and develop clinical talent, deepen educational and community partnerships and elevate awareness of Natividad's clinical quality and distinctive public mission.

The successful candidate will believe deeply in the population Natividad serves.

Monterey County is culturally, economically and linguistically diverse and includes a large agricultural workforce, rural communities, Indigenous-language speakers and residents who face significant barriers to care. More than half of Natividad's patients are covered by Medi-Cal. The needs of this community must remain at the center of the organization's strategy and every major decision.

Candidates should bring at least five years of increasingly responsible health care or hospital administration experience, including three years in a Chief Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer or comparable executive-level role. The successful candidate will have demonstrated experience leading a complex acute care hospital or health system and a strong understanding of hospital operations, finance, clinical services, medical staff relations, regulatory requirements and workforce leadership.

Experience in a public hospital, safety net health system, county-operated organization or similarly complex and politically governed environment is strongly preferred.

Candidates should possess the financial acumen to evaluate operating and capital priorities, understand payer and reimbursement dynamics and ensure the organization's continued long-term sustainability. They must also demonstrate the ability to work constructively with organized labor and to build alignment across stakeholders with differing perspectives and priorities.

The ideal candidate will be an innovative, mission-driven and emotionally intelligent leader with exceptional judgment, integrity and communication skills. This executive will be visible, accessible and collaborative, while also possessing the courage to make difficult decisions and challenge established practices when necessary. Experience working with culturally and economically diverse communities and a genuine commitment to health equity and public service will be essential.

A master's degree from an accredited college or university in Hospital Administration, Health Care Administration, Business Administration, Public Health, Nursing or a closely related field is expected. Candidates may alternatively possess a Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree from an accredited school of medicine.

Equivalent combinations of education, training and experience that demonstrate the required qualifications will also be considered.

This is an exceptional opportunity to lead an organization with a strong foundation, a distinctive mission and a vital role in the future health of Monterey County.

Additionally, the Executive Director is a Senior Vice President for City Year Inc.'s national organization and, therefore, strengthens the connection between City Year's national initiatives and Miami’s local work. As Senior Vice President, the Executive Director also participates within the City Year global network to advance the mission by managing working relationships with staff at City Year's national office and helping to lead and set organizational strategy through network-wide project teams.

About MPU

More Perfect Union is an advocacy, journalism, and education organization with a mission to build power for the working class. They speak directly to young, working class Americans by reporting on the real struggles and challenges of people from a working class perspective and connecting those problems to potential solutions.

Since launching in February 2021, More Perfect Union’s Emmy award-winning coverage has garnered over 6 million followers and subscribers and become the fastest growing, left-of-center YouTube channel. Their work seeks to embolden and empower the working class to engage in building our democracy for the betterment of all working Americans.

About the Position

The Development Director will play a central role in supporting More Perfect Union’s next phase of growth. The person will lead expansion of the development function of one of the fastest growing nonprofit media organizations in the country at a critical time. This is a highly collaborative role, working closely with the Executive Director, Chief Operating Officer, and Editor-in-Chief to advance major donor and foundation fundraising in support of sustainability growing More Perfect Union.

This person will advance the organization's major gift fundraising strategy and directly influence the development of organizational priorities and long-term financial goals. They will also strengthen development systems, and create materials and messaging that are aligned with organizational priorities.

The ideal candidate will have a deep passion for the mission of More Perfect Union and be able to effectively translate that passion into the major gifts fundraising work of the organization. They should be both strategic and detail oriented, comfortable managing multiple workstreams, a great communicator and writer, and excited to help grow major gifts development functions within a fast growing media organization.

Core Responsibilities:

In close partnership with Senior Leadership, plan and lead the organization’s major gift fundraising strategy, including donor prioritization, portfolio management, and donor engagement.
Maintain portfolio of major donors, engage donors in written communication, phone calls, visits and relationship maintenance
Perform regular prospecting for the organization
Manage and support outreach to major donors and foundations, including research, preparation of materials, donor briefings, meeting follow up, and ongoing relationship tracking
Lead the creation, maintenance, and regular updating of written development materials, including pitch decks, donor briefs, grant narratives, and background documents
Develop innovative major donor engagement approaches, solicitation timing, and stewardship priorities to help More Perfect Union continue to expand
Exercise discretion in advising senior leadership on fundraising and development goals, with fundraising projections
Track development activity and progress toward fundraising goals, and help identify opportunities to strengthen and expand support
Scheduling donor meetings as needed
Collaborate across teams to ensure fundraising materials accurately reflect editorial priorities, organizational impact, and future plans
Manage multiple projects simultaneously and meet expected deadlines
Maintain high standard of work in a nimble, fast paced environment
Travel as required for visits
Perform other duties as assigned

Experience/Qualifications:

At least 5 years experience in nonprofit or political fundraising/development at progressive organizations, advocacy groups, or media organizations with at least 3 years experience soliciting major gifts.
Strong writing and editing skills, with experience creating donor facing materials such as decks, proposals, or memos
Experience in principal management
Experience with major donor and foundation fundraising, including relationship management, outreach support and solicitation
Highly organized and detail oriented, with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously
Familiarity with SalesForce or other CRM system
Comfortable working closely with senior leadership and supporting high level fundraising efforts
Ability to be nimble, hustle and flexible
Excitement about building systems and processes in a fast paced, growing organization

4word is a national Christian nonprofit that exists to help women discover and live out
their God-given purpose through faith, work, leadership, and community. Serving women
from early career through the C-suite, 4word creates spaces where women can integrate
their faith with their professional lives rather than feeling they must separate the two.
Under the leadership of CEO Melissa Harrison, the organization is entering an exciting
season of transformation. Following the merger with Polished, the completion of a new
three-year strategic plan, 4word is repositioning itself for national growth while honoring
its founder's legacy. The organization is investing in stronger executive leadership, scalable
programming, and sustainable revenue generation.
The Vice President of Development will join the executive team during a pivotal chapter as
4word expands its Executive Programming, corporate partnerships, membership model,
and national influence. This role is far more than traditional nonprofit fundraising—it
combines development, business development, strategic partnerships, and executive
relationship management to help fuel the organization's long-term vision.

organization's comprehensive revenue growth strategy while serving as a key member
of the executive leadership team.
Reporting directly to the CEO, this leader will oversee donor development, corporate
partnerships, executive business development, sponsorship strategy, and major gift
cultivation. The VP of Development will inherit existing donor relationships while

revenue opportunities.

partners.

prospect opportunities.

● Develop strategic partnerships with ministries, corporations, and
mission-aligned organizations.

jobs.description:
The COO Position

Working alongside the President & CEO, the COO will provide senior operational leadership across the Aquarium, ensuring that day-to-day operations, guest experience, staff experience, infrastructure, technology, financial stewardship, and cross-functional execution are aligned in service of the Aquarium’s mission and strategic priorities.

The COO will lead a portfolio of operational functions directly and will work across the executive team to ensure strong coordination among departments, including areas that may not report directly to the COO. As the Aquarium continues to evolve, the COO’s direct reporting structure may shift to best support organizational needs. Currently, the Acting COO supports a team of five, including the Vice President of Marketing, Communications & Experience, the Vice President of Facilities & Operations, the Senior Director of Capital Projects, the Senior Director of Technology and the Sr. Manager for Dive Operations. The COO also works closely with the Board of Directors, President & CEO and executive team, and represents the Aquarium externally with our government and business partners to advance our operational relationships.

As the aquarium evolves its conservation role and vision, the COO’s strategic leadership and integration will be crucial to bringing all aspects of our conservation model together and ensuring optimal delivery of our services

Essential Functions:

While no two days will look alike, we anticipate the COO will devote their time and attention to the following key priorities:

Strategic Leadership & Execution

Partner with the Board of Directors, President & CEO, and executive team to help shape organizational goals, centering the Aquarium’s mission, values, strategic priorities, and collaborative ways of working.
Translate strategic priorities into clear operating plans, milestones, resourcing decisions, accountability structures, and communication rhythms.
Lead ongoing business review and communication of initiatives, report status on implementation progress, and reduce barriers for operational success and accountability.
Model through daily work how to strategize and lead in manner that integrates and advances our inclusion, and regenerative practices in alignment with our S.A.L.I.S.H. Values.

Operational Leadership

Oversee day-to-day operations of the Aquarium with the executive team, ensuring a high-quality guest experience and staff wellbeing.
Implement and advance sustainable/regenerative and equity-centered practices within the Aquarium and advocate for regenerative and equity-centered marine conservation practices beyond our walls.
Prioritize and integrate collaborative relationships and initiatives with Tribes, local government, and our community partners with Aquarium operations and programs.

Financial Management

Support the development, growth, and management of the Aquarium’s overall budget. Help ensure the Seattle Aquarium values, priorities and needs are represented appropriately in the various budgets.
Identify revenue-generating opportunities and manage expenses in close collaboration with the VP of Finance to ensure the Aquarium meets or exceeds its financial objectives.
Identify opportunities to strengthen operational efficiency, resource stewardship, and organizational sustainability through thoughtful prioritization, technology, process improvement, and cross-functional planning.

Team & Organizational Leadership

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team, fostering a culture of collaboration, clear communication, staff wellbeing, and accountable management.
Lead with curiosity and empathy while developing the skillsets of direct reports, building on their strengths and holding them accountable to their decisions and actions.
Provide mentorship and coaching to executive leaders through change, growth, and development processes while fostering a positive, inclusive, and values-aligned culture.
Partner with the President & CEO and executive team to strengthen leadership practices across the Aquarium, supporting clarity, accountability, collaboration, and staff wellbeing at all levels.
Foster innovation, learning, community engagement, and openness to new, creative, intercultural, and collaborative ideas.
Model the Aquarium’s leadership expectations
Build connections among staff, volunteers, and partners, and actively seek to understand the experiences of members of the Seattle Aquarium community with our institution.
Represent the Aquarium at local, regional, Tribal, and international conferences and events, with the press and media, and through boards, coalitions, and committees.
Serve as a key thought partner to the President & CEO by providing insight rooted in thoughtful analysis of the organization’s operations, finances, and culture, surfacing risks and opportunities early, and offering candid perspective that strengthens decision-making.
To work and engage others in line with the Aquarium’s Mission, D.E.I and S.A.L.I.S.H values.

What You Bring:

Delivering on our bold, urgent mission takes people from every background. The Seattle Aquarium is committed to building a workforce and community rich in diverse identities, languages, cultures, and life experiences. CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER

SPY is looking for a leader who can guide an established youth homelessness organization through its next stage of scale, sustainability, housing growth, public advocacy, and strategic planning. The next leader must have an unwavering commitment to championing SPY's mission and the young people it serves; the ability to adaptively support and develop SPY staff; effectively lead a robust fundraising, external relations, and finance management strategy; and the experience to oversee a complex $15M organization operating 24 hour programs.

ABOUT SAFE PLACE FOR YOUTH

Safe Place for Youth is a leading youth homelessness organization serving young people ages 12 to 25 who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Los Angeles. SPY’s mission is to prevent and end youth homelessness through supportive services, sustainable housing opportunities, community collaboration, and advocacy, with a vision of a socially just and equitable world where all young people are empowered to thrive in self-directed lives and have a safe place to call home.

SPY provides a continuum of youth-centered services that includes street outreach, a drop-in center, case management, education and employment, health and wellness, healing arts, community garden, pregnant and parenting support, shelter, social enterprise, family reunification, housing, and advocacy. In 2025, SPY served more than 1,200 youth, helped 315 young people move into housing, and connected hundreds more to mental health counseling, case management, workforce training, creative arts, street outreach, and other critical supports.

SPY has entered a new stage of organizational complexity and opportunity. The organization now operates 10 sites across the County, including multiple housing programs across shelter, transitional housing, and permanent housing, providing 224 housing resources on any given night. SPY also provides robust supportive services through a field-based model and out of our drop-in center in Venice, including basic needs resources, case management, mental health, substance use counseling, education and employment, pregnant and parenting, healing arts and more.        

The next leader will be called upon to sustain operational excellence across housing and services programs, actively lead a robust fundraising strategy, ensure strong financial oversight, continue SPY’s leadership in advocacy, maintain strong community collaboration, support strong recruitment, retention and development of staff, while keeping the dignity and wellbeing of youth at the center of all of SPY’s work.      

POSITION OVERVIEW

SPY seeks a Chief Executive Officer
to lead the organization into its next phase of impact, sustainability, and public leadership.

The next leader will inherit a respected, mission-driven organization with a strong community identity, a seasoned senior team, an engaged Board, a growing housing portfolio, a newly redeveloped drop-in center, a planned capital campaign, and an urgent opportunity to shape the future of youth homelessness policy and practice in Los Angeles. The role requires a leader who can hold multiple responsibilities at once: stewarding a complex nonprofit enterprise, strengthening internal systems, serving as an external advocate and fundraiser, leading through a new strategic plan, and ensuring that SPY remains deeply connected to the young people and communities it serves.

The successful candidate will be a values-driven, emotionally intelligent, operationally capable, and externally credible leader who can balance ambition with sustainability. They will bring the strategic judgment to decide where SPY should grow, where it should consolidate, where it should advocate, and where it should say no. They will be equally comfortable with youth, staff, donors, elected officials, public agency leaders, community partners, and the Board.
WHAT YOU’LL DO:

Strategic Leadership:
Develop and execute strategic plans in alignment with the organization’s mission, vision, and values. Lead the organization in identifying trends, funding environment, challenges, and future growth opportunities in the housing environment.
Advocacy and Policy Engagement:
Serve as an external champion, advocate, and coalition builder for SPY. Build and maintain strong relationships with elected officials, public agencies, funders, community stakeholders, peer organizations, housing partners, researchers, advocates, neighborhood leaders, and media. Advocate for youth-specific homelessness funding, policy, housing resources, and service models.
Program and Housing Leadership:
Oversee the continued development of SPY’s continuum of care, including outreach, drop-in services, case management, education and employment, health and wellness, healing arts, pregnant and parenting supports, advocacy, shelter, transitional housing, permanent housing, and housing navigation.
Fundraising and Resource Development:

Lead fundraising efforts to secure financial support from diverse sources, including grants, donations, and corporate giving, and other forms of sponsorships.

Cultivate, solicit, and steward relationships with donors, foundations, and corporate partners to expand and diversify the organization's funding base and ensure financial sustainability.

Design expansion and business planning for program expansion. Build partnerships in new areas, establishing relationship with funders and political and community leaders for expansion sites.

Financial Management and Enterprise Sustainability:
Oversee SPY’s financial health in partnership with the CFO, Board Treasurer, Finance Committee, and senior leadership. Ensure strong budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, reserves planning, audit readiness, internal controls, contract compliance, and financial reporting.
Staff Leadership and Culture:
Provide effective leadership and management of staff, volunteers, and consultants that fosters a collaborative and inclusive work environment while still maintaining accountability.
Board Relations and Governance:
Work closely with the Board of Directors to ensure effective board operations, governance, accountability, and transparency. Provide regular updates, reports, and recommendations to the Board to facilitate informed decision-making and strategic planning.
Other duties as assigned to support the mission of the organization.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE YOU’LL NEED:

At least 5 years of executive leadership experience
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; advanced degree or relevant professional training preferred
Significant senior leadership experience in a nonprofit, public agency, housing, social services, youth-serving, advocacy, or mission-driven organization.
Demonstrated commitment to racial equity, social justice, LGBTQ+ inclusion, trauma-informed practice, and youth voice.

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

The Director of Development will direct the overall strategy and fundraising operation on behalf of Johns Hopkins University and for a smaller development office (DOFF), department, area or division. The Director will manage and set goals for a team in support of Johns Hopkins’ ambitious fundraising goals.

The Department of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery currently raises $1M-$2M annually in philanthropic support but is poised for significant growth as it expands its faculty, clinical programs, research enterprise, educational initiatives, and global reach. This role will be responsible for building a proactive and sophisticated fundraising program capable of identifying, cultivating, and securing support from major donors, grateful patients, foundations, alumni, and other philanthropic partners.

The Director of Development will serve as the department’s chief fundraising strategist and build and manage a comprehensive major and principal gifts program. Working in close partnership with Dr. St. John, faculty leaders, grateful patients, alumni, and institutional partners, the Director of Development will develop and execute fundraising strategies that secure critical support for research, education, and patient care, and strategic initiatives.

Founded in 1914, the Johns Hopkins Department of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery has over a century of history in clinical excellence and research innovation. It pioneered American sinus surgery, established the first US temporal bone lab, and is a global leader in cancer care. Today, the department is directed by renowned surgeon and physician-scientist Dr. Maie St. John, MD, PhD, Andelot Professor of Laryngology and Otology.

Bachelor’s degree in Nonprofit Management, Business

revenue goals. Proficiency with donor database management,

Since our founding in 1924, we've cut cardiovascular disease deaths in half, but there is still so much more to do. Natividad is a county-owned and operated public health care system and Level II Trauma Center serving the diverse communities of Monterey County. Each year, Natividad records approximately 60,000 emergency department visits, more than 11,000 inpatient admissions and nearly 2,200 births.

Hospital Chief Executive Officer

Natividad | County of Monterey

Salinas, California

Natividad is a county-owned and operated public health care system and Level II Trauma Center serving the diverse communities of Monterey County. Located in Salinas, California, Natividad provides comprehensive inpatient, outpatient, emergency, diagnostic and specialty care to adults and children, regardless of their ability to pay or immigration status.

Founded in 1886, Natividad has served Monterey County for 140 years and remains one of the region's most important public institutions. The 172-bed hospital is supported by nearly 1,700 employees and more than 400 physicians and medical staff. Each year, Natividad records approximately 60,000 emergency department visits, more than 11,000 inpatient admissions and nearly 2,200 births.

Natividad is fully accredited by The Joint Commission and is one of California's 17 public health care systems. It serves as Monterey County's essential safety net hospital, its only teaching hospital and one of the Central Coast's most important providers of advanced and lifesaving care.

The hospital operates the only Level II Trauma Center in Monterey County, providing 24-hour access to trauma-specialized care and treating approximately 1,400 trauma patients annually. Natividad also offers nationally recognized women's and children's services, a Level III Neonatal Intensive Care Unit affiliated with UCSF Benioff Children's Hospitals, acute rehabilitation, behavioral health, surgical and specialty care, comprehensive primary care and Monterey County's only child maltreatment clinic.

Natividad's longstanding academic affiliation with the University of California, San Francisco is central to its mission. Its nationally recognized UCSF-affiliated Family Medicine Residency is one of the university's original affiliate residency programs and prepares physicians to serve medically underserved communities, advance health equity and become leaders in family medicine.

Natividad is owned and operated by County of Monterey and governed by the County of Monterey Board of Supervisors, with guidance from a Board of Trustees. The Hospital Chief Executive Officer reports directly to the Board of Supervisors and works closely with the Board of Trustees, county leadership, elected officials, labor representatives, community partners and other stakeholders. The CEO will lead an executive team that includes the Chief Medical Officer, Chief Nursing Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Information Officer and Assistant Hospital Administrators.

The incoming CEO will inherit a highly regarded public hospital with a strong financial foundation, a committed workforce and a culture deeply rooted in quality, compassion and service. This is not a mandate to redefine Natividad's identity. Rather, the next CEO will maintain and enhance the organization's strengths while positioning it to respond to a rapidly changing health care, financial and political environment.

The CEO will provide strategic, operational and financial leadership for the hospital and will be responsible for advancing high-quality patient care, long-term sustainability, workforce engagement, regulatory compliance and community impact. The successful candidate will balance fiscal discipline with thoughtful investment, identify opportunities to responsibly grow the organization's reach and strengthen Natividad's position as a trusted provider of choice throughout Monterey County.

This role requires a politically astute and highly collaborative executive who can operate effectively within a visible public-sector governance structure. The CEO must be comfortable working across two boards and building trusted relationships with county officials, legislators, medical staff, employees, organized labor, community leaders, donors and regional health care partners. The successful candidate will be credible in the boardroom, effective in the community and able to communicate clearly in an environment where decisions are subject to public scrutiny.

The Board is seeking a forward-looking leader who can translate vision into action and bring stakeholders together around meaningful change. The next CEO will have the opportunity to advance the patient experience, strengthen access and care coordination, support strategic investments in technology and facilities, attract and develop clinical talent, deepen educational and community partnerships and elevate awareness of Natividad's clinical quality and distinctive public mission.

The successful candidate will believe deeply in the population Natividad serves.

Monterey County is culturally, economically and linguistically diverse and includes a large agricultural workforce, rural communities, Indigenous-language speakers and residents who face significant barriers to care. More than half of Natividad's patients are covered by Medi-Cal. The needs of this community must remain at the center of the organization's strategy and every major decision.

Candidates should bring at least five years of increasingly responsible health care or hospital administration experience, including three years in a Chief Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer or comparable executive-level role. The successful candidate will have demonstrated experience leading a complex acute care hospital or health system and a strong understanding of hospital operations, finance, clinical services, medical staff relations, regulatory requirements and workforce leadership.

Experience in a public hospital, safety net health system, county-operated organization or similarly complex and politically governed environment is strongly preferred.

Candidates should possess the financial acumen to evaluate operating and capital priorities, understand payer and reimbursement dynamics and ensure the organization's continued long-term sustainability. They must also demonstrate the ability to work constructively with organized labor and to build alignment across stakeholders with differing perspectives and priorities.

The ideal candidate will be an innovative, mission-driven and emotionally intelligent leader with exceptional judgment, integrity and communication skills. This executive will be visible, accessible and collaborative, while also possessing the courage to make difficult decisions and challenge established practices when necessary. Experience working with culturally and economically diverse communities and a genuine commitment to health equity and public service will be essential.

A master's degree from an accredited college or university in Hospital Administration, Health Care Administration, Business Administration, Public Health, Nursing or a closely related field is expected. Candidates may alternatively possess a Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree from an accredited school of medicine.

Equivalent combinations of education, training and experience that demonstrate the required qualifications will also be considered.

This is an exceptional opportunity to lead an organization with a strong foundation, a distinctive mission and a vital role in the future health of Monterey County.

Compensation

The current salary range for this position is $439,452 to $599,869 annually. The final compensation package will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, education, skills and organizational needs.

Please note that the classification is currently undergoing a salary review by the County of Monterey and will be communicated as the search progresses.

Position Overview

City Year is seeking an innovative, entrepreneurial, and people-focused leader to serve as the Executive Director (ED) of City Year Miami. This position is an outstanding opportunity to play an integral role in advocating for and advancing public education in Miami. This seasoned executive is responsible for ensuring the site meets its impact, revenue, district partnership, and external relations goals. City Year Miami stands to further its position in the community, and key to the site’s success is a leader and collaborator who is a natural coalition-builder, people developer, and influencer who leads with both tenacity and humility.

Reporting to the Market President, this dynamic, visionary change agent leads 7 staff members and 40 AmeriCorps members serving in 6 partner schools. Additionally, the Executive Director works closely with City Year Miami’s local board, comprised of civic leaders from the public, private, and non-profit sectors. The Executive Director is accountable for a current annual revenue budget of approximately $3MM while simultaneously securing the resources necessary to ensure the sustainability, growth, and scale.

Serving as the primary champion of City Year's impact locally, the Executive Director leads efforts to keep students in school and on track while also ensuring the site's sustainability and continuity. The Executive Director represents City Year Inc. and City Year Miami within the greater Miami community by mobilizing powerful coalitions to catalyze greater educational opportunities for students.

Additionally, the Executive Director is a Senior Vice President for City Year Inc.'s national organization and, therefore, strengthens the connection between City Year's national initiatives and Miami’s local work. As Senior Vice President, the Executive Director also participates within the City Year global network to advance the mission by managing working relationships with staff at City Year's national office and helping to lead and set organizational strategy through network-wide project teams.

Job Description

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree or comparable experience
Commitment to educational equity and belief in the potential of all students
Demonstrated success managing effective and engaged teams, including managing through multiple layers of leadership
Proven skills in influencing and motivating stakeholders; track record in fundraising from corporations, foundations, and major gifts and/or sales
Ability to connect programs to funding, creatively generating other resources, and building collaborative and strategic partnerships
Strong communication, listening, and public speaking skills needed to represent City Year's mission and vision powerfully

Authorized documentation to work in the United States of America 
Criminal background history clearance to work with school-age children, depending on the position

Responsibilities

The Executive Director is responsible for leading and managing site staff and AmeriCorps members to ensure operational success and growth by generating resources and building support from the public and private sectors. This executive serves as a vital link between the local Miami market, the City Year Market Group, and the City Year national office. Site supervision includes the functional areas of student impact and school partnerships, revenue generation, expense management, management and retention of AmeriCorps members and staff, and site board development and relations.

People and Culture: Lead, coach, and develop 7 full-time staff members contributing to high levels of satisfaction, engagement, and retention. Establish a dynamic culture that embodies our core values of inclusivity and teamwork. Further develop site human resources structures to ensure excellent and equitable hiring, performance support, and career advancement practices.
AmeriCorps Member Experience: Ensure the site delivers a transformational experience for all City Year AmeriCorps members by supporting members in feeling prepared and confident in their service and promoting member persistence from initial confirmation of acceptance to completion of service.
Student Impact: In partnership with senior site staff and regional support staff, the ED will ensure high quality and commitment to the nationally developed Whole School, Whole Child service delivery model implemented by City Year AmeriCorps members in partner elementary, middle, and high schools.
Private Sector Fundraising, Cultivation, and Stewardship: Serve as the chief fundraiser leading site staff and local advisory board to motivate key influencers to generate the resources necessary to meet annual and long-term goals leveraging national revenue and stewardship strategies. Collaboration: Connects with stakeholders to identify shared interests; partners with others to incorporate different perspectives toward a common goal.
Teamwork: Actively contributes to shared projects with the understanding that team success is personal success.
Understanding & Building Connection: Considers perspectives of others and cultivates relationships to strengthen interpersonal bonds with colleagues and external stakeholders.

Learning: Strives to continuously develop and improve self, teams, and organization.

Exercise discretion in advising senior leadership on fundraising and development goals, with fundraising projections
Track development activity and progress toward fundraising goals, and help identify opportunities to strengthen and expand support

Collaborate across teams to ensure fundraising materials accurately reflect editorial priorities, organizational impact, and future plans

Maintain high standard of work in a nimble, fast paced environment

The COO Position

Working alongside the President & CEO, the COO will provide senior operational leadership across the Aquarium, ensuring that day-to-day operations, guest experience, staff experience, infrastructure, technology, financial stewardship, and cross-functional execution are aligned in service of the Aquarium’s mission and strategic priorities.

The COO will lead a portfolio of operational functions directly and will work across the executive team to ensure strong coordination among departments, including areas that may not report directly to the COO. As the Aquarium continues to evolve, the COO’s direct reporting structure may shift to best support organizational needs. Currently, the Acting COO supports a team of five, including the Vice President of Marketing, Communications & Experience, the Vice President of Facilities & Operations, the Senior Director of Capital Projects, the Senior Director of Technology and the Sr. Manager for Dive Operations. The COO also works closely with the Board of Directors, President & CEO and executive team, and represents the Aquarium externally with our government and business partners to advance our operational relationships.

As the aquarium evolves its conservation role and vision, the COO’s strategic leadership and integration will be crucial to bringing all aspects of our conservation model together and ensuring optimal delivery of our services

Essential Functions:

While no two days will look alike, we anticipate the COO will devote their time and attention to the following key priorities:

Strategic Leadership & Execution

Partner with the Board of Directors, President & CEO, and executive team to help shape organizational goals, centering the Aquarium’s mission, values, strategic priorities, and collaborative ways of working.
Translate strategic priorities into clear operating plans, milestones, resourcing decisions, accountability structures, and communication rhythms.
Lead ongoing business review and communication of initiatives, report status on implementation progress, and reduce barriers for operational success and accountability.
Model through daily work how to strategize and lead in manner that integrates and advances our inclusion, and regenerative practices in alignment with our S.A.L.I.S.H. Values.

Operational Leadership

Oversee day-to-day operations of the Aquarium with the executive team, ensuring a high-quality guest experience and staff wellbeing.
Implement and advance sustainable/regenerative and equity-centered practices within the Aquarium and advocate for regenerative and equity-centered marine conservation practices beyond our walls.
Prioritize and integrate collaborative relationships and initiatives with Tribes, local government, and our community partners with Aquarium operations and programs.

Financial Management

Support the development, growth, and management of the Aquarium’s overall budget. Help ensure the Seattle Aquarium values, priorities and needs are represented appropriately in the various budgets.
Identify revenue-generating opportunities and manage expenses in close collaboration with the VP of Finance to ensure the Aquarium meets or exceeds its financial objectives.
Identify opportunities to strengthen operational efficiency, resource stewardship, and organizational sustainability through thoughtful prioritization, technology, process improvement, and cross-functional planning.

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team, fostering a culture of collaboration, clear communication, staff wellbeing, and accountable management.

Provide mentorship and coaching to executive leaders through change, growth, and development processes while fostering a positive, inclusive, and values-aligned culture.
Partner with the President & CEO and executive team to strengthen leadership practices across the Aquarium, supporting clarity, accountability, collaboration, and staff wellbeing at all levels.
Foster innovation, learning, community engagement, and openness to new, creative, intercultural, and collaborative ideas.
Model the Aquarium’s leadership expectations
Build connections among staff, volunteers, and partners, and actively seek to understand the experiences of members of the Seattle Aquarium community with our institution.
Represent the Aquarium at local, regional, Tribal, and international conferences and events, with the press and media, and through boards, coalitions, and committees.

To work and engage others in line with the Aquarium’s Mission, D.E.I and S.A.L.I.S.H values.

Delivering on our bold, urgent mission takes people from every background. The Seattle Aquarium is committed to building a workforce and community rich in diverse identities, languages, cultures, and life experiences. Candidates will be evaluated on the full range of their lived and learned experience and core competencies, including:

Passion for the Aquarium’s mission, of Inspiring Conservation of our Marine Environment and commitment to advancing the Aquarium’s SALISH values .
10+ years of proven senior leadership experience in a complex, mission-driven, and/or visitor-serving organization, ideally including nonprofit, aquarium, zoo, museum, cultural institution, conservation, or public-facing operations experience, with a successful track record of creating operational excellence.

CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER

SPY is looking for a leader who can guide an established youth homelessness organization through its next stage of scale, sustainability, housing growth, public advocacy, and strategic planning. The next leader must have an unwavering commitment to championing SPY's mission and the young people it serves; the ability to adaptively support and develop SPY staff; effectively lead a robust fundraising, external relations, and finance management strategy; and the experience to oversee a complex $15M organization operating 24 hour programs.

ABOUT SAFE PLACE FOR YOUTH

Safe Place for Youth is a leading youth homelessness organization serving young people ages 12 to 25 who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Los Angeles. SPY’s mission is to prevent and end youth homelessness through supportive services, sustainable housing opportunities, community collaboration, and advocacy, with a vision of a socially just and equitable world where all young people are empowered to thrive in self-directed lives and have a safe place to call home.

SPY provides a continuum of youth-centered services that includes street outreach, a drop-in center, case management, education and employment, health and wellness, healing arts, community garden, pregnant and parenting support, shelter, social enterprise, family reunification, housing, and advocacy. In 2025, SPY served more than 1,200 youth, helped 315 young people move into housing, and connected hundreds more to mental health counseling, case management, workforce training, creative arts, street outreach, and other critical supports.

SPY has entered a new stage of organizational complexity and opportunity. The organization now operates 10 sites across the County, including multiple housing programs across shelter, transitional housing, and permanent housing, providing 224 housing resources on any given night. SPY also provides robust supportive services through a field-based model and out of our drop-in center in Venice, including basic needs resources, case management, mental health, substance use counseling, education and employment, pregnant and parenting, healing arts and more.        

The next leader will be called upon to sustain operational excellence across housing and services programs, actively lead a robust fundraising strategy, ensure strong financial oversight, continue SPY’s leadership in advocacy, maintain strong community collaboration, support strong recruitment, retention and development of staff, while keeping the dignity and wellbeing of youth at the center of all of SPY’s work.      

POSITION OVERVIEW

SPY seeks a Chief Executive Officer
to lead the organization into its next phase of impact, sustainability, and public leadership.

The next leader will inherit a respected, mission-driven organization with a strong community identity, a seasoned senior team, an engaged Board, a growing housing portfolio, a newly redeveloped drop-in center, a planned capital campaign, and an urgent opportunity to shape the future of youth homelessness policy and practice in Los Angeles. The role requires a leader who can hold multiple responsibilities at once: stewarding a complex nonprofit enterprise, strengthening internal systems, serving as an external advocate and fundraiser, leading through a new strategic plan, and ensuring that SPY remains deeply connected to the young people and communities it serves.

The successful candidate will be a values-driven, emotionally intelligent, operationally capable, and externally credible leader who can balance ambition with sustainability. They will bring the strategic judgment to decide where SPY should grow, where it should consolidate, where it should advocate, and where it should say no. They will be equally comfortable with youth, staff, donors, elected officials, public agency leaders, community partners, and the Board.
WHAT YOU’LL DO:

Strategic Leadership:
Develop and execute strategic plans in alignment with the organization’s mission, vision, and values. Lead the organization in identifying trends, funding environment, challenges, and future growth opportunities in the housing environment.
Advocacy and Policy Engagement:
Serve as an external champion, advocate, and coalition builder for SPY. Build and maintain strong relationships with elected officials, public agencies, funders, community stakeholders, peer organizations, housing partners, researchers, advocates, neighborhood leaders, and media. Advocate for youth-specific homelessness funding, policy, housing resources, and service models.
Program and Housing Leadership:
Oversee the continued development of SPY’s continuum of care, including outreach, drop-in services, case management, education and employment, health and wellness, healing arts, pregnant and parenting supports, advocacy, shelter, transitional housing, permanent housing, and housing navigation.
Fundraising and Resource Development:

Lead fundraising efforts to secure financial support from diverse sources, including grants, donations, and corporate giving, and other forms of sponsorships.

Cultivate, solicit, and steward relationships with donors, foundations, and corporate partners to expand and diversify the organization's funding base and ensure financial sustainability.

Design expansion and business planning for program expansion. Build partnerships in new areas, establishing relationship with funders and political and community leaders for expansion sites.

Financial Management and Enterprise Sustainability:
Oversee SPY’s financial health in partnership with the CFO, Board Treasurer, Finance Committee, and senior leadership. Ensure strong budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, reserves planning, audit readiness, internal controls, contract compliance, and financial reporting.
Staff Leadership and Culture:
Provide effective leadership and management of staff, volunteers, and consultants that fosters a collaborative and inclusive work environment while still maintaining accountability.
Board Relations and Governance:
Work closely with the Board of Directors to ensure effective board operations, governance, accountability, and transparency. Provide regular updates, reports, and recommendations to the Board to facilitate informed decision-making and strategic planning.
Other duties as assigned to support the mission of the organization.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE YOU’LL NEED:

At least 5 years of executive leadership experience
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; advanced degree or relevant professional training preferred
Significant senior leadership experience in a nonprofit, public agency, housing, social services, youth-serving, advocacy, or mission-driven organization.
Demonstrated commitment to racial equity, social justice, LGBTQ+ inclusion, trauma-informed practice, and youth voice.
Ability to embody SPY’s values of care, community, inclusivity, innovation, integrity, and sustainability.
Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage complexity, and build organizational infrastructure.
Experience with fundraising, external relations, public funding, and     institutional partnerships.

Demonstrated adaptive and situational leadership, and experience mentoring and developing teams. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Past success working with a Board of Directors with the ability to cultivate board member relationships

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

Physical effort/lifting, up to 15-20 pounds at times.

new_jobs.title: Executive Director - Highland Health Associates
new_jobs.description:
When you join the growing BILH team, you're not just taking a job, you’re making a difference in people’s lives.

Reporting to the Highland Board of Directors and a designated Hospital Leader, this senior position is responsible for strategic planning and overall operations of Highland. Strategic planning responsibilities include physician retention and growth, leadership development and Board support, annual planning, oversight of the Business Support and Value-Based Entity programs, serving as the primary liaison and advocate with the senior team at Highland’s affiliated contracting and population health organization (Network), and as the primary contact with external professional advisors. The Executive Director assures that all governing documents are current and consistent with Highland’s strategic direction. Responsible for all planning aspects of Highland’s Annual Membership Meeting and the annual Board of Directors elections. Assures that Highland members are well-informed of contracts, services, requirements, and other matters through ongoing meetings, written communications, and the Highland IPAConnect website platform. Negotiates non-network payer contracts on behalf of the Highland physicians and other members. Develops the operating budget, monitors revenue and expenses, and oversees risk payer settlement distributions. Personnel management includes three Managers, among other staff. Serves as the Privacy Officer of the company

Job Description

JOB FUNCTIONS

Strategic Planning - Responsible for:
A. PCP membership stability (retention) and PCP growth
B. Leadership development and succession planning, in collaboration with Highland Board of Directors and its Executive Committee.
C. Board of Directors and Executive Committee support, including all aspects of meeting preparation and follow-up.
D. Developing the Annual Planning document, in collaboration with the Managers.
E. Oversight of the Highland Business Support Program including adding new value-added services and coordinating launch programs.
F. Oversight of the Highland Value-Based Entity (VBE) Program including regulatory, financial and operations oversight of the VBE Program.
G. Development of new innovative programs, as needed, to support Highland practices.
Primary Liaison with Affiliated Contracting Organization/Population Health Network (Network)
A. Responsible for ongoing general communications, problem solving, and private practice advocacy, serving as the Highland “voice” for our practices
B. Negotiates Network Affiliation Agreement and infrastructure funding.
C. Committee and work group representation could include Growth, Funds Flow, Contracting, Pediatric Governance, Network Policy Review, and Administrator Meetings.
D. Explore and develop new Network affiliation, as necessary, in collaboration with the Board of Directors and its Executive Committee including Request-for-Proposal (RFP) development and process oversight, and Black Box Analysis of financial arrangements
Winchester Highland Management (HM) Oversight and Collaboration - Includes the

joint supervision of the HM Manager with the designated Hospital Senior Leader. Assist, as

needed, with annual budget development and renewal of insurance policies. Hold weekly

collaborative meetings with the Managers. Serve as HM Privacy Officer.

Finance and Insurance – Responsible for:
A. Development of the annual Operating Budget for Board approval. Monitor changes in revenue and expenses, reforecasting the budget, as needed.
B. Oversight of internal Accountant
C. Annual insurance renewals (Directors & Officers, Errors & Omissions, Cyber, Property, and Workers Compensation)
D. Lease Renewal, as needed. Responsible for maintenance of physical office space.
E. Risk Contract Funds - Development of Funds Flow Mechanics and oversight of settlement funds distributions.
Governing Documents
A. Develop and maintain Highland’s By-laws, Clinician Services Agreement (CSA), and

organizational policies such that these governing documents are current, internally

consistent and reflective of both Highland’s strategic direction and applicable Network

documents.

B. Assure that Highland Board and Executive Committee actions and decisions are aligned

with these organizational documents.

C. Collaborate with Legal Counsel and the Highland Board of Directors on any necessary amendments to the By-Laws and CSA. Responsible for the planning and oversight of the amendment processes.
D. Organizational Policies – develop and update policies, as needed.
E. Annual Conflict of Interest (COI) and Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDA) – renew COIs and NDAs annually for Board of Directors, Medical Directors, Committee Members, and
management staff. Raise any discrepancies with these policies and agreements with the Board of Directors or its Executive Committee.
Payer Contracting
A. Negotiate and renew non-Network Payer Agreements assuring adequacy and fairness of physician, other clinician, and Highland reimbursement for services provided.
B. In collaboration with Legal Counsel, assure that contract language is fair, reasonable, and consistent with applicable regulatory requirements.
HIPAA Privacy Officer

As the HIPAA Privacy Officer for Highland and HM, responsible for Privacy & Security

Policies; staff training; Business Associate Agreements; collaboration with Security

Officer/Consultant, BILH Privacy & Security Team, and Privacy & Security Legal Counsel;

and, breach response, as necessary.

Serve as Primary Contact with External Advisors – includes Legal Counsels, Tax

Accountant, and Security Consultant.

Annual Membership Meeting and Elections
A. Responsible for planning and oversight for the Annual Membership Meeting including

setting the agenda, coordinating with internal and external outside speakers, and preparing

the presentations and talking points for Highland presenters.

B. Annual Board Elections – Coordination and oversight of the Nominating and Elections

Processes consistent with the Highland By-Laws.

Personnel Management – Responsible for interviewing, hiring, disciplinary action as

necessary, training and coaching for assigned staff.

Qualifications

Education

Required:
Bachelor’s degree

Preferred:
Master’s degree in Business, Healthcare Administration, or related field

Experience

Required:
At least 7 years of progressively responsible related experience, including personnel management

Preferred:
10 years of progressively responsible related experience

Other Skills/Knowledge

Required:
Demonstrated passion for the private practice of medicine, strong customer service skills, well-developed verbal and written communication skills, and capacity to advocate and negotiate with tact, diplomacy and conviction.

Preferred: Contracting with payers and contracting organizations, Physician retention and growth

Other Job Requirements

Professional Commitment Requirements: N/A

On-call Requirement: N/A

Schedule Requirements: Generally, Monday through Friday business hours.

Flexibility with early morning or evening meetings required. Hybrid remote and in office model.

Travel Requirements: N/A

Reports to the Highland Board of Directors and its Executive Committee, and a designated senior leader at the Hospital. Current direct reports are:

Quality & Performance Improvement Manager
Provider & Payer Relations Manager
EMR/HIE Manager (co-management role with the Hospital)
Internal Accountant
